findings.title: Success criteria coverage
findings.description:
Every criterion has an implementation task and, where testable, a test task:
- **SC1–2:** Tasks 1.1 and 1.2.
- **SC3–4:** Task 1.3, with tests in 1.4.
- **SC5:** the round-trip test in Task 1.4.
- **SC6–9:** Tasks 2.1 and 2.2, with tests in 2.3.
- **SC10:** Task 3.2, with the mock test in 3.4.
- **SC11:** Task 3.4.
- **SC12:** Tasks 4.1 and 4.2.
- **SC13:** Tasks 3.5 and 5.1.
- **SC14:** Task 5.2.

The slice restates no NFR, so no load test or CI gating task is required.

findings.title: Sequencing and test-with pattern
findings.description: The order config → enforcement module → wiring → shipped configs respects dependencies, with no cycles. Each implementation group is immediately followed by its test task (1.4, 2.3, 3.4). The required-kwarg change in Task 3.1 and its call-site fixes (3.3, 3.4, 3.5) land inside one commit, so no commit leaves the suite broken.

findings.title: Integration tests do not pin `dt`, so the reflect-flip test can fail as written
findings.description:
`SimulationManager` takes `dt` as a constructor argument (`src/migratory_server/simulation.py:63`), and the server passes `1.0 / tick_rate` (`src/migratory_server/server.py:129`). Task 3.4's shared setup never states a `dt`.
- **Reflect flip:** `test_reflect_policy_flips_velocities_at_edges` puts an agent at `(99, 50)` with velocity `(10, 0)` and steps once. It only crosses `x = 100` if `dt > 0.1`; at any `tick_rate` above 10 the assertion `vx < 0` fails.
- **50-step tests:** the OPEN drift test has the same dependency on start offset, speed and `dt`.

Add an explicit `dt` (e.g. `dt=1.0`) or start positions and speeds that guarantee crossing to the shared setup.

findings.title: Commit markers are checkboxes in standalone tasks, and the 4.3 commit is at an untested point
findings.description:
- **Format:** all five commits (Tasks 1.5, 2.4, 3.6, 4.3, 5.5) are written as `- [ ] **Commit:** ...` inside their own "Commit" tasks. Markers must be plain `**Commit**:` lines, never checkboxes. Convert each to a plain line at the end of its section and drop the five commit tasks.
- **Untested point:** Task 4.3 (lines 283-286) commits the `policy: wrap` change to both shipped configs after only a `python -c` load check. The full suite does not run until Task 5.1. `tests/test_config.py:45` loads `config/default.yaml` and `tests/test_main.py:70` starts the server on it, so the behaviour change should be tested before the commit. Move the Task 5.1 `pytest` run ahead of the 4.3 commit.

findings.title: Walkthrough can leave `config/test.yaml` off `wrap`, breaking SC12
findings.description: Task 5.2 steps 6–7 edit `config/test.yaml` to `reflect`, then `open`. Step 8 says to restore "whichever policy you want to keep (recommend `wrap`)". SC12 requires `wrap`, so this is not optional. Nothing afterwards checks the file, and Task 5.5 stages only docs, so a stray edit stays in the working tree. Change step 8 to "restore `policy: wrap` and confirm `git diff config/test.yaml` is empty".

findings.title: Task file is overweight for a 2/5 slice
findings.description:
The file has 22 tasks, five commits and about 30 named tests for one enum, one field, one roughly 40-line module and one call site. Suggested cuts and merges:
- **Merge 1.1 and 1.2:** a three-line enum and a one-line field in the same file.
- **Merge 4.1 and 4.2:** the same one-line YAML edit and the same verify command.
- **Drop 5.1:** it duplicates 3.5; one full-suite run after the config change is enough.
- **Trim tests in 2.3:** drop the "dispatches and does not raise" parametrized test (line 171), which every other test already covers. Merge the two OPEN no-op tests, and parametrize the four reflect edge tests.
- **Drop the "Confirm" step in 3.2 (line 209):** "zero import-time … overhead" is not verifiable and contradicts the Notes (line 329), which say the import is unconditional. The mock test in 3.4 already proves the behaviour.
- **Fold commits:** the Section 4 commit can join Section 3's or the final one; three or four commits suffice.

findings.title: Round-trip test asserts less than SC5 states
findings.description: SC5 says reloading the emitted YAML "produces an equal `ServerConfig`". `test_bounds_policy_yaml_round_trip` only asserts that the policy matches. Asserting `reloaded == original` as well would cover the criterion as written at no extra cost.

findings.title: Viewer steps in Task 5.2 are not completable by an AI implementer
findings.description: Steps 5–7 need visual observation in the Three.js viewer. SC14 is defined as manual, so this follows the slice. A headless equivalent would let the implementer check these off: a short WebSocket client that samples snapshots for 30–60 seconds and checks positions against the bounds.

findings.title: Frontmatter says `status: complete` while every checkbox is unchecked
findings.description: The file is marked complete, and `src/migratory_server/bounds_enforcement.py` already exists, but no task is checked off. Either the status or the checkboxes are stale. Task 5.3 also instructs setting this same field to `complete`.

findings.title: CHANGELOG and status tasks do not trace to a success criterion
findings.description: Tasks 5.3 and 5.4 are ordinary slice housekeeping, and the startup log line in Task 3.3 traces to walkthrough step 4. None is scope creep worth cutting. Task 3.5 names `test_force_builder.py` and `test_clients.py` as likely call sites; the one it does not name is `tests/test_repulsor_integration.py:53`, which the "any other file" clause and the pytest run will catch.
